claims.text: Additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components can contain fabrication-induced defects.
Additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components can exhibit dimensional inaccuracies.
A composition-tailored post-fabrication heat treatment will improve dimensional precision relative to no post-fabrication heat treatment.
A composition-tailored post-fabrication heat treatment will improve mechanical integrity relative to no post-fabrication heat treatment.
A composition-tailored post-fabrication heat treatment will reduce fabrication-induced defects relative to no post-fabrication heat treatment.
The post-fabrication heat treatment will refine the alloy microstructure.
The post-fabrication heat treatment will reduce residual stresses.
The post-fabrication heat treatment promotes phase stabilization.
The post-fabrication heat treatment refines grain boundaries.
Reduced residual stress will reduce warping or distortion and thereby improve dimensional accuracy.
Heat-treatment-induced phase stabilization and microstructural refinement will increase tensile strength.
Heat-treatment-induced phase stabilization and microstructural refinement will increase ductility.
The heat treatment will reduce porosity.
The heat treatment will reduce microcracks.
The proposed effects are expected only for alloy compositions that permit phase stabilization and microstructure refinement through heat treatment.
The proposed effects are expected only when additive manufacturing has not excessively degraded the material.
The magnitude of improvement may depend on alloy composition and additive-manufacturing parameters.
